[MUQATIL:5:28-31/r1] MUQATIL, d. 150 · author | holds | Habil says he will not raise his hand to kill his brother because he fears God, Lord of the worlds.
[MAJAZ:v1p160/r3] MAJAZ, d. 209 · author | holds | Basatta ilayya yadaka means you extended your hand toward me.
[MAJAZ:v1p160/r4] MAJAZ, d. 209 · author | holds | Tabūʾa bi-ithmī wa-ithmika means to bear my sin and your sin; elsewhere it means to admit a sin, kill someone in retaliation, or arrive at a lodging. ʿAmr b. Ḥunā’s verse illustrates the blood-for-blood usage.
[ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p187#2/r3] ABDURRAZZAQ, d. 211 · قتادة | reports | Qatāda explains the threatened return with both sins as the sin of killing me and your own sin.
[TAB-FULL:v8p328/r1] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · author | holds | The victim says that if his brother extends his hand to kill him, he will not extend his own hand to kill his brother.
[TAB-FULL:v8p328/r2] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · عبد الله بن عمرو | reports | ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr says the victim was the stronger of the two, but scruple kept him from raising his hand against his brother.
[TAB-FULL:v8p328/r3] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · ابن عباس | reports | Ibn ʿAbbas glosses the victim’s words as refusing to retaliate and resolving to keep his hand from his brother.
[TAB-FULL:v8p328/r4] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · مجاهد | reports | Mujahid says scripture commanded that a person whom another sought to kill should leave him unresisted.
[TAB-FULL:v8p328/r5] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · author | prefers | Al-Ṭabarī prefers that both brothers were forbidden to kill unjustly; the victim’s words express his own refusal to commit the equally forbidden murder. No evidence shows he knew of the threat in time to defend himself; scholars report he was killed asleep, and the verse does not command passivity.
[TAB-FULL:v8p328/r6] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · author | holds | He fears God’s punishment if he extends his hand to kill his brother.
[TAB-FULL:v8p328/r7] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · author | holds | “Lord of the worlds” means the owner of all creatures, who can punish him for raising his hand to kill.
[ZAJJAJ:v2p166/r6] ZAJJAJ, d. 311 · يقال | reports | It is said that swords were forbidden then, as in Muhammad's Meccan period and in Jesus's time.
[ZAJJAJ:v2p166/r7] ZAJJAJ, d. 311 · author | holds | The speaker says he will not retaliate, fight, or kill his brother because he fears the Lord of all worlds.
[THALABI:v4p50/r1] THALABI, d. 427 · عبد الله بن عمر | reports | Ibn ʿUmar swears that the murdered brother was the stronger of the two, but scruple kept him from raising his hand against his brother.
[THALABI:v4p50/r2] THALABI, d. 427 · مجاهد | reports | Mujahid says that at that time a person threatened with murder was commanded to leave the attacker and not resist.
[MAWARDI-FULL:v2p29/r1] MAWARDI-FULL, d. 450 · author | holds | Abel means that if Cain starts the killing, Abel will not initiate the same against him.
[MAWARDI-FULL:v2p29/r2] MAWARDI-FULL, d. 450 · ابن عباس | reports | Ibn Abbas and Ibn Umar say Abel refrained from defending himself out of scruple, despite having the ability and legal permission.
[MAWARDI-FULL:v2p29/r3] MAWARDI-FULL, d. 450 · مجاهد | reports | Mujahid and al-Hasan instead say Abel was not permitted to resist the person who intended to kill him.
[WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p337/r1] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · ابن عباس وحذيفة | reports | Ibn Abbas and Hudhayfa explain: if you begin by trying to kill me, I will not be the one who begins by killing you.
[WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p337/r2] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · الحسن ومجاهد | reports | Al-Hasan and Mujahid say it was prescribed for people at that time to let an attacker kill them rather than resist.
[WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p337/r3] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · author | holds | A person defending himself must use the least force needed and aim to repel, not kill; if killing the attacker is the only possible defense, it is allowed, though a victim may choose to submit to unjust death.
[WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p337/r4] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · عثمان | reports | The source says Uthman acted by submitting rather than killing an unjust attacker.
[WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p337/r5] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · رسول الله | reports | The Prophet instructed Muhammad ibn Maslama to cover his face with his sleeve and be God's slain servant rather than God's killer.
[WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p337/r6] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · author | holds | The verse shows that one facing a would-be murderer may not raise a hand with the intention of killing; any action must intend to repel.
[WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p337/r7] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · عبد الله بن عمرو | reports | Abd Allah ibn Amr says the slain brother was the stronger man, but scrupulous fear of God kept him from raising his hand against his brother.
[WAHIDI-WAJIZ:5:27-30/r5] WAHIDI-WAJIZ, d. 468 · author | holds | Even if Cain begins to kill him, Abel will not initiate murder because he fears God.
[JISHUMI:v3p1932/r5] JISHUMI, d. 494 · author | holds | Bast is extension, the opposite of contraction, as spreading is opposite to folding.
[BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p43/r1] BAGHAWI-FULL, d. 516 · author | holds | بسطت means you extended or stretched your hand.
[BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p43/r2] BAGHAWI-FULL, d. 516 · عبد الله بن عمر | reports | Ibn Umar says the victim was the stronger of the two men, but scrupulous fear kept him from raising his hand against his brother.
[BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p43/r3] BAGHAWI-FULL, d. 516 · author | holds | Under Adam’s law, a person threatened with murder could submit and endure to seek reward; the author compares this to Uthman.
[BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p43/r4] BAGHAWI-FULL, d. 516 · مجاهد | reports | Mujahid says they were commanded at that time not to resist if someone intended to kill them, but to be patient.
[KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p658/r4] KASHSHAF-FULL, d. 538 · مجاهد | reports | Mujāhid and others say Abel was stronger but refrained and surrendered from fear of God, since self-defense was not permitted under that law.
[KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p659/r2] KASHSHAF-FULL, d. 538 · author | holds | The conditional uses a verb but its answer uses a nominal participle to convey that Abel will not do an act that earns the vile description; the bāʾ reinforces the negation.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p178#2/r3] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · مجاهد | reports | Mujahid says people at that time were commanded neither to draw a sword nor to resist someone who sought to kill them.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p178#2/r4] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · عبد الله بن عمرو وجمهور الناس | reports | Abdullah ibn Amr and the majority say Abel was stronger than Cain but refrained scrupulously.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p178#2/r5] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · author | prefers | Ibn Atiyya prefers the strength-and-scruple view: Abel's restraint suggests Cain was a sinner rather than an unbeliever, since scruple would make no sense otherwise; the scrupulous person accepts oppression for afterlife reward, as Uthman did.
[TABRISI:5:28-29/r1] TABRISI, d. 548 · author | holds | Basṭ means extension or spreading out, the opposite of contraction.
[TABRISI:5:28-29/r10] TABRISI, d. 548 · author | holds | Hābil says he fears God if he stretches his hand to kill his brother.
[TABRISI:5:28-29/r5] TABRISI, d. 548 · author | holds | The lām in la-in is an oath lām, and its answer is mā anā bi-bāsiṭ; mā cannot be a conditional answer, and the prior oath answer takes precedence.
[TABRISI:5:28-29/r6] TABRISI, d. 548 · author | holds | Hābil answers his brother's threat: if you extend your hand to kill me, I will not extend mine to kill you.
[TABRISI:5:28-29/r7] TABRISI, d. 548 · الحسن، مجاهد، الجبائي | reports | Al-Ḥasan and Mujāhid, as preferred by al-Jubbāʾī, say defensive killing was not permitted then; Hābil was commanded to endure so God Himself would exact justice.
[TABRISI:5:28-29/r8] TABRISI, d. 548 · ابن عباس وجماعة | reports | Ibn ʿAbbās and others say Hābil meant he would not initiate wrongful aggression; they say Qābil murdered him stealthily while he slept by dropping a rock on him.
[TABRISI:5:28-29/r9] TABRISI, d. 548 · المرتضى | prefers | Al-Murtaḍā finds the apparent sense different from both readings: if his brother reaches to kill him, Hābil will not wrong him, since self-defense is permissible to escape harm without intending to kill.
[IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p334/r1] IBNJAWZI-ZAD, d. 597 · ابن عباس | reports | Ibn Abbas understands the statement as meaning that the speaker would not retaliate to defend himself.
[IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p334/r2] IBNJAWZI-ZAD, d. 597 · عكرمة | reports | Ikrima understands it to mean that the speaker would not initiate the attack.
[IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p334/r3] IBNJAWZI-ZAD, d. 597 · ابن عمر وابن عباس | reports | Ibn Umar and Ibn Abbas say scruple kept him from defending himself, although he could do so and self-defense was permitted.
[IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p334/r4] IBNJAWZI-ZAD, d. 597 · الحسن ومجاهد | reports | Al-Hasan and Mujahid say defending oneself was not lawful at that time.
[IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p334/r5] IBNJAWZI-ZAD, d. 597 · ابن جرير | reports | Ibn Jarir says the verse does not prove the victim knew the murderer's intention and chose not to defend himself; reports say he was killed treacherously, so the text alone cannot establish that claim.
[RAZI-FULL:v11p162#3/r1] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | holds | Razi asks why Abel did not defend himself even if defense was obligatory or at least lawful; he answers that Abel addressed Cain before the attack to admonish him and deter intentional murder.
[RAZI-FULL:v11p162#3/r2] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | reports | A report says Cain waited until Abel slept, then killed him by striking his head with a large stone.
[RAZI-FULL:v11p162#3/r3] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · أهل العلم | reports | Scholars say a defender must use the least force necessary and intend to repel the attack, not to kill; killing is permitted only if no lesser defense succeeds.
[RAZI-FULL:v11p162#3/r4] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | reports | Some say a person may choose to submit to being killed; Uthman did so, and the Prophet told Muhammad ibn Maslama to cover his face and be killed rather than kill.

[BURHAN:v3p379/r4] BURHAN, d. 794 · author | holds | The second clause uses an active participle instead of a finite verb to make the comparison apt; with the sound obstacle gone, it follows the usual object order.
[BURHAN:v3p379/r5] BURHAN, d. 794 · author | holds | The word order reflects the contrast: the first brother is eager to aggress and is expressed with a verb, while the other denies aggression and is expressed with a participle.
